subject: plant parents
one_liner: A cartridge-based home console for keeping your houseplants alive, with permadeath enabled by default.
brand_voice_notes: Hardware-company deadpan. Perennia discusses a fern the way a console manufacturer discusses a launch title: bays, region codes, save architecture, firmware revisions, service intervals. It never once acknowledges that what it is telling the customer is that a plant died. Every sentence is either a specification or a support policy. Warmth exists only as the tone of a manual. No winking, no whimsy, no exclamation marks, and no acknowledgement that a console for houseplants is an unusual object to manufacture.

hero.h1: Your monstera is a save file you keep losing.
hero.sub: Perennia is a cartridge-based home console for keeping houseplants alive. One plant per cartridge. One save slot per cartridge. There are no cloud saves, and the manual explains why across four of its forty-four pages.

features.title: One plant, one cartridge
features.blurb: Every plant in your home ships as a physical cartridge, moulded to fit exactly one bay. Adding a fern means buying a fern. Cartridges are region-locked to your hardiness zone and will not boot at a friend's house, which we consider correct behaviour.

features.title: Permadeath ships enabled
features.blurb: When a plant dies, the save is erased at the cartridge level rather than the console. Competing systems let you roll back a drought. We evaluated that feature for two years, built it twice, and removed it both times.

features.title: Difficulty is assigned, not chosen
features.blurb: The console reads the light in the room and sets the difficulty itself. Fiddle-leaf fig has never been rated below EXPERT in any household, in any season. The rating is written to the cartridge and cannot be lowered by you, by us, or by an authorised service centre.

pricing_tiers.name: Starter Bay
pricing_tiers.tagline: Ships with a plant that was going to survive anyway.

pricing_tiers.name: Four-Bay Household
pricing_tiers.tagline: For homes running more than four plants concurrently.
perks: Pest encounters: spider mites, scale, thrips
Second controller for a roommate who will not use it

pricing_tiers.name: Estate Cartridge
pricing_tiers.tagline: The save file outlives the player.
perks: Succession planning for up to thirty cartridges
A named beneficiary written into every save
A technician visits the house twice a year
No restoration after death. This includes yours.

testimonials.quote: It rated the fiddle-leaf fig EXPERT before I got it out of the car. I bought it anyway. The console has not mentioned it since, which is somehow worse than being told.
testimonials.name: Denise Okonjo-Frame
testimonials.title: Assistant Manager, Regional Tile and Grout Showroom

testimonials.quote: My wife keeps her saves on the second bay. We have agreed not to look at each other's playtime, and the console does not offer a way to enforce that.
testimonials.name: Rob Vandermeer
testimonials.title: Certified Pool Operator, Level II

testimonials.quote: The light meter said my apartment was insufficient for the medium I had selected. It was right. It said so every ninety seconds for eleven days.
testimonials.name: Priya Raman-Holt
testimonials.title: Nights and Weekends Veterinary Reception Lead

demo_screen_concept: A cartridge-select screen rendered as the console faceplate: a row of six moulded bays, five loaded with plant cartridges (Monstera, Pothos, Fiddle-Leaf Fig, ZZ, String of Pearls) and one empty and unlit. Selecting a bay boots that cartridge into a dot-matrix LCD panel below, which shows the save file as blocky pixel readouts: a segmented moisture bar, hours of playtime, days since last save, an assigned difficulty locked at its rating, a light-level meter, and three tabs (STATUS / INVENTORY / ACHIEVEMENTS). A WATER button writes to the save and intermittently returns SAVE FAILED: SOIL ALREADY SATURATED. Inventory lists consumables with counts. Most achievements are locked and rendered as dashes. A RESET SAVE control opens a confirmation that has to be held down, and the empty bay shows a NO CARTRIDGE boot error.

design_direction.style: Injection-moulded home console shell, showroom daylight mode. The page is staged as the product literature and retail faceplate of a consumer electronics manufacturer that has decided a houseplant is a software title and a fern is a save file. One warm moulded-ABS ground (#DCD7C6) runs the entire page with no dark mode, no glass, no backdrop blur, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no felt panels, no foil bands, no banknote plates, no vellum scribe lines, no enamel keylines, no drafting grid and no wall labels. This is the first entry in recent memory that permits a shadow, and it permits exactly one: a hard 4px offset black shadow with zero blur, the flat drop shadow of a moulded part photographed against a showroom wall, applied only to raised plastic surfaces and never to type. Every other surface effect is banned. Nothing has a border radius above 3px except the console corner, which is 10px, because that is the radius the tooling cuts. The organising move is the shell: every major section is a moulded panel one step lighter than the ground (#E7E3D5) sitting inside a 2px ink keyline with a hard offset shadow, capped by a moulding seam, a 3px ink rule that runs the full width of the panel with a 24px notch cut out of it where the section number sits, so sections arrive as parts that came out of a mould rather than as cards that came out of a template. The core motif is the cartridge: a tall rectangle with a chamfered top-left corner, a 6px ink label band across its upper third carrying a title in condensed technical caps, and two moulded grip ridges down its right edge, built entirely in CSS with clip-path and repeating-linear-gradient, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the pricing tier badge and the testimonial portrait frame, so every discrete item on the page reads as something you physically slot in. The second motif is the screen: a recessed dot-matrix panel, a dark olive well (#2B3126) inset with a 3px ink bezel and overlaid with a pixel grid built from two repeating-linear-gradients at 3px pitch, carrying pale phosphor type (#A9BC80) in a true bitmap face, used for every readout, every telemetry figure and the whole demo, so the only place on the page where the product speaks is behind glass. The third motif is the moulding stamp: a small ink circle containing a recycling-style numeral with a date code beside it in bitmap type, dropped in the bottom-right corner of every shell panel, marking the part rather than selling it. Chakra Petch sets the wordmark, headlines and every specification label in squared technical caps at monumental sizes with the confidence of a manufacturer that prints tolerances on the box, tracking tightened to -0.02em at display sizes, flush left against the moulding seam. Fira Sans carries plain manual body copy at 17px with a 1.6 line-height and a 66-character measure, exactly as set in a spiral-bound instruction booklet. Silkscreen, a genuine bitmap face, is quarantined strictly to the dot-matrix screens: save data, playtime, moisture percentages, difficulty ratings, date codes and tier prices, always inside a recessed olive well, never on the plastic, so bitmap type never appears anywhere a real console would have used a printed label. One rationed cartridge magenta (#A8145C) is quarantined strictly to loss telemetry (erased saves, permadeath notices, plants no longer running, the EXPERT rating, days since last save once it goes critical, the withheld line in pricing) and appears nowhere decorative, so the only saturated colour on a beige page is always the console reporting a death. Motion is hardware-restrained: panels seat 4px down into their shadow on hover like a part pressed into its housing, cartridges translate 6px down into a bay on hover and never scale, the dot-matrix screens boot once on reveal by stepping their pixel grid from 0 to full opacity over 220ms with no fade, CTAs invert to an ink flood with beige type knocked out and depress 2px on press, magenta counters step once on entering the viewport and then hold, sections fade up 6px on a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur, no gradients on type, no neon, no glow, no scanline overlays on the whole page, no CRT curvature, no bento lattice, no drafting hairline grids, no rubrication, no versals, no guilloché, no lathe rules, no leg bands, no chenille patches, no title blocks, no dimension lines, no split-flap numerals, no emoji. Reads like a hardware company that files your fern under 'title' and considers its death a save-data event.

fonts.body: 'Fira Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Consumer hardware product page issued as retail product literature: a showroom hero with a monumental squared-caps claim beside a product photograph of the console and a boot-screen telemetry panel in bitmap type, three moulded feature panels indexed by CSS cartridges, three testimonial panels with cartridge-framed directory portraits and owner registration codes, a three-tier configuration table laid out as a moulded parts schedule rather than floating cards, a closing specification band, and a handoff to the cartridge-select demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Hardware seating, not animation. Panels press 4px into their hard offset shadow on hover; cartridges slide 6px down into a bay and never scale; dot-matrix screens boot by stepping their pixel grid opacity from 0 to full in 220ms with no cross-fade; primary CTAs invert to an ink flood and depress 2px on press; magenta loss counters step once on entering the viewport and then hold; sections fade up 6px on a 40ms stagger. Every transition is 180 to 260ms on ease-out. Everything is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns at 1200px, asymmetric at 7:5. Left column: a letterspaced model-number eyebrow in bitmap type inside a small olive well, then the h1 in Chakra Petch at clamp(2.6rem, 6vw, 4.6rem) flush left against the moulding seam, the sub at a 58-character measure, then a two-button row with the ink-flood primary CTA and a hairline secondary linking to the demo. Right column: the console product photograph seated inside a 2px ink keyline with the hard 4px offset shadow, and directly beneath it a recessed dot-matrix boot panel running four save-telemetry lines in phosphor bitmap type with the days-since-last-save figure in cartridge magenta. Below both columns, a full-width moulding seam and a row of four specification cells separated by 2px ink rules.

images.rationale: Hero earned it: this is a hardware product page and the whole conceit is a physical moulded console, so a studio product shot of the console beside a pothos does work no CSS shell could. Demo assets skipped because the demo is a dot-matrix LCD cartridge-select screen, which is pixel-shaped rather than photo-shaped and would be ruined by a photograph. Remaining budget went to three testimonial headshots, shot as stiff employee-directory portraits on the same beige ground so they sit inside the CSS cartridge frames without fighting the palette.

items.judge: pass: beige moulded ABS console with dark recessed cartridge bay and an unlit dot-matrix panel, pothos in terracotta alongside, warm neutral palette matches #DCD7C6 ground exactly, no text or logo artifacts
items.prompt: Studio product photograph of a boxy beige injection-moulded home game console from the mid 1990s, sitting on a warm grey-beige seamless studio backdrop (#DCD7C6), shot from slightly above at a three-quarter angle. The console is plain textured ABS plastic with softly rounded corners, one dark recessed cartridge bay on its top face, two flat unmarked buttons, and a small dark rectangular dot-matrix display panel that is switched off. A small potted pothos plant in a plain unglazed terracotta pot sits directly beside the console, its trailing leaves resting across the console shell. Even soft studio lighting, one gentle contact shadow pooled under each object, background falling off softly. Muted warm neutral palette only: beige plastic, terracotta, deep charcoal #1E1D24 recesses, dusty green leaves, no saturated colour anywhere. Editorial hardware product photography, medium format, crisp plastic texture and visible mould seams. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no brand marks, no labels, no rendered UI screens.
